response_format.description: auto returns inline when small and switches to paged delivery when the response exceeds max_inline_bytes. full disables automatic paging. paged forces paged delivery.

max_inline_bytes.description: Maximum serialized structuredContent size to return inline when response_format is auto.

page_size_bytes.description: Maximum JSON text fragment size per page when paged delivery is used.

include_json_content.description: When false, omit duplicated JSON from text content and rely on structuredContent.

assignment_item.description: Value assignment for INSERT/UPDATE. Creates WRITE lineage.

source_attributes.description: If value comes from another attribute

operator.description: Filter operator. Vector operators: L2_DISTANCE uses <->, COSINE_DISTANCE uses <=>, NEGATIVE_INNER_PRODUCT uses <#>. These vector operators are also valid for join-like comparisons.

sub_filters.description: Nested filters for OR groups or EXISTS subqueries

implementation_status.description: Implementation workflow status shared by entities, processors, and processor UX.

processor_info.description: Processor metadata returned by MCP read tools.

processor_name.description: Logical/business processor name. For api_server processors, use the user-facing API name; do not use HTTP method/path or code identifiers.

module_name.description: Physical/code identifier. For every class-backed processor in a Spring Boot Application model, use the simple class name without package (OrderController), including processor_general. Keep verified package_name, qualified_class_name and source_file in other_info for tracing. module_name must be unique within the model physical-name namespace; package metadata does not bypass this. Reuse one class/module across roles rather than creating duplicates. Do not use a route, HTTP verb or method name as the Controller class name. For api_server use the verified single-operation identifier (operationId, controller method or function), never a server/router grouping.

other_info.description: Optional verified source and processor-specific metadata. Controller/API routing is stored in other_info.endpoints; explicit endpoints input takes precedence over nested endpoints and legacy method/path. Filter matchers, Interceptor include/exclude paths and Controller Advice scope are not HTTP endpoints. Omit unknown values.

package_name.description: Verified source package, without the class name. Omit if unknown.

qualified_class_name.description: Verified fully qualified class name for source tracing; module_name remains the simple class name.

source_file.description: Verified source file path. Never fabricate a path from a class name.

matchers.description: Filter applicability conditions, not endpoints. Use only verified matchers.

order.description: Verified Filter or Interceptor execution order.

controller_scope.description: Verified Controller Advice applicability, preserving source selector meaning. Omit unknown scope.

exception_types.description: Verified exception types handled by Controller Advice.

endpoints.description: Verified inbound HTTP routes for a Controller class or API Server boundary. One Controller processor can contain multiple path/method/handler combinations. Omit unknown fields; never assume GET or derive routes from class names. On update omission preserves, an array replaces, [] empties, null clears. Do not use for Filter/Interceptor matching or Advice scope. Stored only in other_info.endpoints; the top-level response is a projection, not a separate stored value. API Server represents one Swagger/OpenAPI operation: endpoints is an array with at most one method/path pair. Different methods or paths require separate processors. Spring Controller classes may have multiple endpoints. Endpoint cardinality follows the storage catalog: is_module=true permits multiple endpoints; false, null or omitted permits at most one. Clients cannot override this flag. This applies to all processor types and both endpoints and other_info.endpoints. Check acceptable_processors or processor_storage_types before writing. Legacy JSON strings encoding an array or null are also accepted, decoded and validated; new writes store arrays or null and top-level endpoints read projections use arrays or null. Existing raw other_info may retain legacy strings until updated. New clients must send arrays. Invalid strings are rejected without clearing metadata.

path.description: Verified request mapping path; resolve class and handler mappings only from evidence.

method.description: Verified HTTP method; omit if unspecified or unknown. Never default to GET.

handler.description: Actual source handler method name without class/package prefix; omit if unknown.

endpoint_id.description: Server-assigned stable Controller endpoint ID. Preserve on edits to retain the contract association.

input_attribute_id.description: Server-managed Controller INPUT Object ID. Preserve on edits; do not invent. Same-handler routes share this ID.

output_attribute_id.description: Server-managed Controller OUTPUT Object ID. Preserve on edits; do not invent. Add verified child fields under this Object.

processor_storage_type.description: Exposed as processor_storage_type, sourced from ENTITY_TYPE

exposure_level.description: TARA exposure level. 0 = Not defined/follow model exposure level, 1 = Isolated, 2 = Internal, 3 = Partner, 4 = External, 5 = Public. Omit this or set 0 when the processor should follow the model exposure level; set it only when the processor exposure differs from the model.

sub_type.description: Optional free-text refinement of the storage type; alias subType. Examples: controller REST/MVC, service Application/Domain/Facade/AI Service, repository Repository/DAO/Mapper/Memory Repository. See model_selection_guide for the complete recommended Spring subtype catalog; do not create new default types for internal stages.

layer_id.description: Existing layer assignment. Creation sets NULL; property updates preserve it.

output_attribute_id.description: Server-managed Controller OUTPUT Object ID. Preserve on edits; do not invent. Add verified child fields under this Object.

use_lookup.description: Catalog policy; false permits INPUT and OUTPUT only. Existing LOOKUP data remains readable.

io_policy.description: Storage-type IO rules and Controller endpoint contract reminders.

projection_item.description: SELECT column mapping. Defines how a source attribute becomes a target attribute. This is the primary source of READ and TRANSFORM lineages. Wildcards such as '*' or 'alias.*' are authoring shorthand only and must not be sent as a single projection item. Use explicit SQL select items with beyond_add_transformation_by_sql so lineage can be created per column. Within one SELECT transformation, each projected source column must map to its own distinct target attribute unless you are using explicitly modeled nested child attributes.

projection_type.description: DIRECT=simple copy, FUNCTION=date/string func, VECTOR_DISTANCE=vector similarity/distance expression such as embedding <-> :query_embedding or COSINE_DISTANCE(embedding, :query_embedding), VECTOR_COMPARISON=boolean vector threshold expression such as embedding <-> :query_embedding < 0.8, AGGREGATE=SUM/COUNT in SELECT, COALESCE=null handling

source_attributes.description: Source attributes. Empty for COUNT(*) or literals. Do not use a single representative source attribute for '*' or 'alias.*'; wildcard projections must be expanded into the full relevant attribute list.

examples._description: Vector distance projection from pgvector/PostgreSQL/Supabase SQL
Boolean vector threshold projection from pgvector SQL

Wildcard caution: expand 'p.*' into one projection per relevant column before sending. If the result is an internal rowset on the current processor, prefer LOOKUP targets over collapsing all columns into one OUTPUT attribute.
Invalid pattern: do not collapse different source columns into one row/object container attribute such as admin_user.

raw_expression.description: Original ORDER BY expression, including vector distance expressions such as d.embedding <-> :query_embedding.

source_attribute.description: A universal attribute reference. source_entity_id can point to a Table, File, Redis Key, Processor, or any other entity.

source_alias.description: Optional alias used in SQL (e.g., 'o', 'c', 'p'). If omitted, the server fills it from the source entity table/module name when possible.

source_model_id.description: Beyond Entity model ID. Optional if source_attribute_id or source_entity_id is provided; the server will resolve it when possible.

target_attribute.description: Reference to a target entity/processor attribute. target_alias and target_model_id may be omitted; the server will resolve them from the target entity/attribute when possible. For transformation projections or aggregations targeting the current processor, if target_attribute_id is omitted but target_entity_id and target_column_name are provided, the server may reuse an existing LOOKUP/OUTPUT attribute by column name or create a new LOOKUP attribute and populate target_attribute_id.

target_alias.description: Optional alias for the target entity or processor scope. If omitted, the server fills it from the target entity table/module name when possible.

target_column_name.description: Target column or attribute name. Required when target_attribute_id is omitted. For projections/aggregations into the current processor, this name is also used to resolve or auto-create a LOOKUP attribute.

target_attribute_id.description: Target attribute ID. Optional when target_entity_id and target_column_name are provided and the server can resolve or auto-create the target attribute.

target_model_id.description: Beyond Entity model ID. Optional if target_attribute_id or target_entity_id is provided; the server will resolve it when possible.

transformation.description: The logic engine of Beyond Entity. Maps data flow between Entities (Tables, Files, Caches) and Processors. Every transformation item automatically generates a Lineage record.

transformation_name.description: Human-readable name, e.g., '[T1] Fetch active orders'

semantic_level.description: (Optional) Semantic level of the transformation, which can guide how lineages are generated and visualized. RELATIONAL is traditional table-based operations. DOCUMENT is for document stores like MongoDB. KEY_VALUE is for key-value stores like Redis. GRAPH is for graph databases like Neo4j. VECTOR is for vector search or vector-distance operations such as pgvector similarity queries.

referring_raw_code.description: (Optional) Original SQL or code. Kept for reference and debugging.

other_info.description: (Optional) Additional information related to the transformation. json object where you can put any properties relevant to this transformation, such as database connection info, API endpoint info, code generation hints, etc.

sources.description: Source entities used in this transformation (FROM clause)

projections.description: SELECT mappings (for SELECT) or value expressions (for INSERT SELECT)

examples.referring_raw_code: SELECT o.order_id, o.total FROM orders o WHERE o.status = 'ACTIVE' AND o.created_at >= :startDate
INSERT INTO coupon_issue (coupon_id, customer_id, status, issued_at) VALUES (:coupon_id, :customer_id, 'ISSUED', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)

examples._description: SELECT login candidate with one projection target per selected column
examples.referring_raw_code: SELECT id, username, password_hash, role FROM admin_users au WHERE au.email = :email AND au.is_active = TRUE

examples._description: SELECT with JOIN, aggregation, and grouping
examples.referring_raw_code: SELECT DATE_TRUNC(:groupBy, o.created_at) AS period, COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(o.amount) AS total_amount FROM orders o WHERE o.created_at >= :startDate GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC(:groupBy, o.created_at)

value_info.description: Value specification for filters and assignments

value_type.description: LITERAL=fixed value, PARAMETER=processor INPUT/LOOKUP, ATTRIBUTE=another entity column, EXPRESSION=complex SQL

value.description: For LITERAL: the value. For PARAMETER: :param_name format

value_entity_id.description: For PARAMETER: processor_id. For ATTRIBUTE: entity_id

comparison_operator.description: Optional comparison operator for compound expressions such as vector distance threshold filters. Example: lt for '<'.

comparison_right_operand.description: Optional right operand for compound expressions such as vector distance threshold filters. Example: 0.8 in 'embedding <-> :query_embedding < 0.8'.
